concepts.label: mcstat
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept anywhere in the registry or extraction layer. First-contact tool connecting directly to the KV/memcached port to retrieve node-, bucket-, or cluster-wide statistics.

concepts.label: port 11210 (KV / memcached)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - mcstat's default connection port when none is specified.

concepts.label: User impersonation (Server diagnostic CLI)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept for this capability anywhere in the registry or extraction layer. mcstat's -I/--impersonate option lets the connecting administrator run a stats request as if it were a different named user.

relations.subject: tool:mcstat
relations.evidence: If no port number is specified, either a number specified with the \-p option, is used, or the default 11210 is used.

relations.subject: tool:mcstat
relations.evidence: \-I or \--impersonate <username>                                                      | Try to impersonate the specified user.

notable_absence.finding: mcstat's own -h[=statkey] flag is documented as able to output, per statkey, 'descriptions and indications of the stat's scope and required privileges' - meaning the tool itself is aware of a privilege model for individual stats - but the reference page never names a single privilege string or ties any specific statkey to the RBAC/privilege catalogue used elsewhere in this corpus's REST reference pages. The entire privilege surface is deferred to the tool's own --help output at runtime rather than documented in prose. Consistent with this round's authorship-provenance hypothesis: the sentence reads like a feature description written by the engineer who built the --help flag, not a TW who then went and filled in the actual privilege names in a table.

cross_component_finding: mcstat's -b/-a bucket-scoping and -j/-J JSON-output options closely mirror the already-promoted tool:cbstats's own interface (both connect over port 11210, both take -b/-a and -u/-P/-I-style credential flags), yet neither this page nor cbstats-intro.md cross-references the other. A missed xref opportunity, and the kind of gap expected from tool-owner-authored pages that were never run through a unifying cross-linking review pass.
cross_product_finding: mcstat connects directly to the raw KV/memcached port on a specific node (11210 by default) - a connectivity model Capella does not expose to customers, who cannot reach individual data nodes' memcached ports directly. This entire mc* tool family (mcstat, mctestauth, mctimings) is implicitly Server (self-managed)-only, though no page in the batch states that restriction outright.
